title: What you put behind the switch: payloads
objective: Match the four payload families (reporters, sensors, actuators, ablation) to the question each one answers.

steps.title: The driver picks the cell; the payload picks what you do to it
steps.body:
Once [[Cre]] defines the cell, a Cre-dependent payload decides the experiment. Four families cover most work:

- **Reporter** (tdTomato, GFP) — *see* the cells and their endings.
- **Sensor** (GCaMP) — *watch* them fire (calcium).
- **Actuator** (ChR2/optogenetics; [[hM3Dq]]/[[hM4Di]] [[DREADD|DREADDs]]) — *drive or silence* them.
- **Ablation** (diphtheria-toxin receptor + DTX; Cre/[[Flp]]-dependent Caspase3) — *delete* them to test necessity.

steps.prompt: Match each payload to the question it answers.
pairs: Where are these cells and their endings?
What happens if I drive or silence them?
steps.explanation: Look, watch, drive, delete — the four verbs of a mouse-genetics experiment.

steps.prompt: You want to test whether a colon afferent subtype is NECESSARY for a high-force distension behavior. Which payload?
options: A reporter such as tdTomato to visualize the neurons
A calcium sensor such as GCaMP to watch their activity
An ablation tool (DTR+DTX or Caspase3) to remove them
A brighter GFP variant for clearer imaging of them
steps.explanation: Necessity = remove the cells and see if the behavior is lost. Ablation tools do that. (Silencing with hM4Di is a reversible alternative — covered in C5.)

steps.title: Bred-in vs. delivered by virus
steps.body: A payload can be **bred in** (a knock-in allele, like the Rosa26 reporters) or **delivered by [[AAV]]**. Cre-dependent viral payloads are written **[[DIO]]** or **FLEX** (double-[[loxP|floxed]] inverted ORF) — same on/off logic, but injected where you want it. This is the bridge to the viral-tools and DREADD units (C4, C5).

sources.citation: Wolfson RL, et al. DRG afferents... distal colon. Cell 186:3368-3385 (2023).
sources.note: Uses reporters, GCaMP imaging, optogenetic actuators, and ablation — all four payload families.
